question: Can an observable-seeded block Krylov projection retain the full finite-grid nonlinear contact-energy response with a calculated residual bound and useful total cost?
scope: Synthetic finite-model engineering; no biological validation, new protein prediction or continuum certification. Compact/elongated geometries have not previously had nonlinear references computed in this project.

domain_check.scope: Reference-only diagnostic at the same spacing as33/4; does not establish full thermal-basin coverage.

basis.seed: Every centered equilibrium-weighted original quartic node energy divided by its fixed all-mode native harmonic SD.
basis.method: Block Arnoldi/Krylov with two full reorthogonalization passes and SVD of the residual block. Rebuild for every geometry, stiffness and grid with the same procedure.
basis.early_stop: First checkpoint whose calculated bound passes all three times and all observables, before accessing full response. Never choose rank by measured reference error.
basis.breakdown: If the next residual block is numerically dependent, stop and report the achieved invariant subspace or unresolved residual.
basis.equilibrium_null: Original equilibrium weights; no refitting or coordinate truncation.

bounds.integrated: Duhamel Cauchy-Schwarz residual integral, and two-sided triangular-domain residual bound when orthogonality assumptions hold; report projection and finite-arithmetic diagnostics separately.
bounds.claim: Analytic finite-model inequalities evaluated in floating point; no interval-arithmetic certificate.

timing: Count input geometry, native Hessian/scales, equilibrium quadrature, sparse operator, basis, residual bounds, projected exponentials and all3 response reconstructions. Compare cold and total three-time-query costs against full sparse expm_multiply. Do not amortize unless explicitly reported as a separate reuse scenario.
reference: Independent full sparse matrix exponential action on the same nonlinear finite generator. Compare development cases against saved v0.3.0 archives when available.
comparison: Original full three-coordinate operator versus projection; previous low-frequency failures retained as history.
query_order: All approximate ranks/bounds first, then full reference.
failure: Any failed required finite fidelity/bound/cost gate rejects a general pass across the tested range. Grid/domain failures leave continuum resolution unresolved even if the finite projection passes. Keep every case and all unsuccessful checkpoints. Stop at budget without enlarging it after observing outcomes.
heldout_rule: The construction and thresholds are fixed before compact/elongated response calculations; each basis may access its own model/operator/observables, not any saved response.
